main_body: 4x3 block of sci-fi metal panel tiles; each 16px tile has a lighter upper plate with rivets and a darker lower plate separated by a dotted seam
top_band: lighter blue-grey plate, rows ~0-8 of each tile, then a dotted seam and a darker lower band
evidence: The tiles are terrain/wall-face autotile pieces, not standing objects. Each tile shows a lighter upper plate, a dotted seam acting as a front edge, and a darker lower face. The centre column tiles have an inset dark-edged recess. Judged leniently for terrain, so it passes, but it is borderline because the 'top' is more a plate division than a true foreshortened surface.

style.evidence: The panels use about 4 blue-grey steps with dark blue-tinted outlines, not pure black, which is acceptable. Rivets and seam dots add some detail. Large plate areas (5x5 px or more) are one flat colour with no grain, unlike the reference grass tufts and per-stone shading in the paving. The cyan lights are a nice accent, but the surface is flatter and thinner than the reference, so it fails.
